Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and procurement teams are working through the Order Form and we need to confirm a couple of items before we proceed to signatures:

1) Data residency: we require all inference logs and customer content to remain in EU regions for the lifetime of the contract. Is there any part of the observability pipeline (traces, metrics, ephemeral logs) that might be routed outside EU?

2) Retention: Fabrica needs a bespoke retention option: 90 days for inference request payloads, 365 days for aggregated usage metrics, and a 30-day grace period after contract termination to allow for data export. Can these be reflected in the Order Form?

3) Deletion: we need assurance that on-request deletion (by API or ticket) triggers physical deletion within X days. Please confirm timelines for: soft-delete, immediate KV cache purge, and permanent removal from backups.

- EU-only residency: yes, we can pin your tenant to EU regions only; no telemetry will be routed outside the EU for customer content or request logs if you select the EU residency option on the order form.
- Bespoke retention windows: we support configurable retention windows per account. 90/365/30 as you listed are feasible; we need to capture this as an Order Form amendment so it becomes binding.

Permanent deletion from primary storage occurs within 30 days by default; backups are rotated on a 90-day schedule unless you opt into an accelerated backup purge (can be 7/30/90 days with pricing impact).

Hi all — technical confirmation and clarifications:

1) Residency: when Fabrica opts for EU-only tenancy we deploy customer data and logs to our eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 clusters (depending on capacity). Control plane metadata (tenant identifier, billing pointers) is stored in our control plane region but does not include PII or content. We can include a contractual clause: "Customer Content and Request Logs will be stored and processed only within the European Economic Area (EEA)."

2) Retention semantics:
- "Request payloads" = raw inference inputs and outputs (90 days). Marked for soft-delete upon request; soft-delete prevents queryable access immediately.
- "Aggregated usage metrics" = anonymized totals and billing counters (365 days).
- "Grace period after termination" = 30 days for export. After that, data is scheduled for purge.

3) Deletion mechanics and timelines:
- API request/ticket received -> immediate soft-delete (0–24 hours)
- KV cache purge -> immediate on soft-delete
- Primary storage permanent purge -> default 30 days after soft-delete; can accelerate to 7 days for an additional fee (we list as an order form optional add-on)
- Backups: standard rotation is 90 days; we can commit to expedited backup purge within 30 days for enterprise customers with explicit SLA (requires HSM/KMS key lifecycle coordination).

4) Evidence: we can provide a deletion runbook and a flow diagram (see redwood-data-deletion-flow.png attached) and include a right-to-audit clause in the amendment.

Happy to review the proposed redline and suggest precise language for the Order Form.

-Mina
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

1) Residency clause: Acceptable as written — we will state EEA-only processing for Customer Content and Request Logs. Control plane metadata language will be limited to operational identifiers only.
